# Colony Law Basics
The [bold]Colonial Civil Code[/bold] governs every civilian and non-military person on the colony. This page covers the essentials; the [textlink="full code" link="AU14CCLaw"] has every crime and sentence.
## Ground Rules - Everyone must obey colonial law and follow lawful safety orders during emergencies, evacuations, quarantines and security events. - [bold]Spirit of the law[/bold]: laws are meant as they're intended, not by their exact wording. - Marshals and administration may use discretion on minor offenses. Law enforcement's own offenses may not be ignored. - Proportional self-defense is legal. - Credibly threatening a major or capital crime can be charged as that crime. A credible threat to kill is charged as attempted murder. - Colonial law is civilian law. Military procedure doesn't apply unless martial law is lawfully declared. - Law enforcement can't be used to enforce corporate policy, except lawful safety orders and emergency directives. Corporate policy never overrides criminal law. - Law enforcement may refuse unlawful orders.
## Who's in Charge From highest to lowest: 1. Civilian Court or Arbiter
2. Colony Administrator
3. Chief Marshal
4. Deputy or Acting Administrator
5. Colony Marshals
6. Deputized Security
If a court is active, it has the final say on criminal cases. If not, the Marshal's Office handles arrests, charges and sentencing.
## Classes of Crime - [bold]Minor crimes[/bold]: public nuisance, trespassing, petty theft, public intoxication and similar. Usually 5 to 8 minutes, and can be handled with a citation. - [bold]Major crimes[/bold]: disorderly conduct, major vandalism, assault, manslaughter and similar. Usually 10 to 20 minutes. - [bold]Capital crimes[/bold]: murder, attempted murder, mass casualty sabotage and similar. Punished by permanent confinement, loss of weapon licenses and any office, possible exile, and possibly execution. - [bold]Add-on charges[/bold] such as resisting arrest or aiding and abetting are added to the base sentence.
## Weapons Law Owning a weapon is a licensed privilege. - [bold]Class A, civilian tools[/bold] (knives, crowbars, work tools): legal unless used to threaten, brandished, carried into restricted areas or used in a crime. - [bold]Class B, civilian firearms[/bold] (pistols, shotguns, hunting rifles): need a Colonial Firearm License. No open carry in public without authorization. - [bold]Class C, restricted weapons[/bold] (automatic weapons, explosives, flamethrowers and the like): illegal for civilians. Only for the military, Marshals, authorized security and emergency militias. - [bold]Class D, prohibited weapons[/bold] (chemical, biological or radiological weapons, improvised explosives): illegal for everyone.
## Confinement That Isn't a Crime [bold]Precautionary confinement[/bold] protects the colony without charging anyone: - someone who is a danger to themselves or others, until medically cleared - someone at risk of spreading contamination, until cleared - enemy combatants and prisoners of war - protective custody, for someone's own safety
## Emergencies - Colonial Administration can issue emergency orders during a genuine colony-wide danger: curfews, lockdowns, evacuations, quarantines, rationing and similar. - In a colony-wide emergency, the Acting Administrator or the Marshal can form a [bold]civilian militia[/bold]. Militias follow colonial law, report to them, can't arm from official stockpiles without authorization, and can't dress as police.
## Courts and Executions - A court can be convened for major or capital crimes, disputed arrests, abuse of authority or corporate misconduct. The judge can't have been involved in the case, can't be the accused's direct superior, and can't know the accused or victim personally. - Executions are only for capital crimes, after a full trial judged by an Arbiter, and need the joint approval of the Acting Administrator, the Marshal and the judge.
